title: Topic 10 | Non-uniform motion along a circle

questions.text: A material point moves uniformly along a circle. What is the angle between its velocity and acceleration vectors?

A car travelled around a circle of radius 50 m, covering the arc corresponding to 40° at 4 m/s, the arc of 60° at 6 m/s, the arc of 70° at 7 m/s, and the remaining part at 8 m/s. Find the average speed of the car over the whole circle (km/h).
A body moving along a circle has an initial angular velocity of 3 rad/s and an angular acceleration of 0.1 rad/s². Through what arc angle does it move in 0.5 s?

A material point moving along a circle with uniform angular acceleration has an initial angular velocity of 3 rad/s and an angular acceleration of 0.1 rad/s². Find its angular velocity after 5 s (rad/s).

A material point moving along a circle with uniform angular acceleration has an initial angular velocity of 4 rad/s and an angular acceleration of 0.2 rad/s². Find its angle of rotation after 4 s (rad).
A body moves along a circle with an angular velocity given by the equation ω = 2 + 0.5t. How many revolutions does it make in 20 s?

A body with an initial angular velocity of 3 rad/s and an angular acceleration of 0.5 rad/s² moves along a circle with uniform angular acceleration. If the radius of the circle is 5 dm, find the linear speed after 6 s (m/s).
Find the linear speed after 20 s of a material point that started from rest and moves along a circle with an angular acceleration of 0.4 rad/s² (m/s). The radius of the circle is 5 m.
How is the instantaneous velocity vector directed in curvilinear motion?
answers: The direction of the instantaneous velocity cannot be determined in such motion
Along the tangent to the trajectory
Along the tangent to the radius of the curve
Along the radius of the curve, away from the centre

questions.text: As a body moves along the trajectory AB, its velocity changes from v₁ to v₂. How is the average acceleration vector directed?
answers: Along the direction of vector v₁
Along the direction of vector v₂
From the tip of vector v₂ to the tip of vector v₁
From the tip of vector v₁ to the tip of vector v₂

questions.text: The tangential acceleration of a body is 5 m/s² and its total acceleration is 10 m/s². Find its centripetal acceleration (m/s²).
A material point moves uniformly along a circle of radius 3 m with an angular velocity of 4 rad/s. Find its tangential acceleration (m/s²).

A material point moves along a circle of radius 20 cm with uniform angular acceleration and a tangential acceleration of 5 cm/s². How long after the start of motion will its normal acceleration be 2 times its tangential acceleration?
If the tangential acceleration of a body is 6 m/s² and its centripetal acceleration is 8 m/s², what is its total acceleration (m/s²)?
The angle between the velocity and acceleration of a material point moving on a horizontal surface is π/3. What is the nature of the point's motion?

A material point moves along a circle of radius 4 m with uniform angular acceleration, with an initial angular velocity of 2 rad/s and an angular acceleration of 2 rad/s². Find the ratio of its normal acceleration to its tangential acceleration after 5 s.

Point A on the rim of a wheel of diameter 100 cm was rotating uniformly at a speed of 6 m/s. What is the angle (in degrees) between the velocity vector and the acceleration vector of point A 2.5 s after braking began?

Point A on the rim of a wheel of radius √3 m was rotating uniformly at a speed of 4.2 m/s. What is the angle (in degrees) between the velocity vector and the acceleration vector of point A 0.4 s after braking began?

The speed of point A of a wheel relative to the ground is 3 m/s. The speed of point C relative to the ground is −2 m/s. The diameter of the circle is 1 m. Find the centripetal acceleration of the points on the wheel rim (m/s²).

Point A on the rim of a wheel of diameter 100 cm was rotating uniformly at a speed of 4.8 m/s. What is the angle (in degrees) between the velocity vector and the acceleration vector of point A 0.6 s after braking began?
